name: Larry Ellison
title: The Dropout Who Skipped Version One
subtitle: Handed to relatives at nine months and told he would amount to nothing, he quit college twice, put in $1,200, and built Oracle from a research paper no company had turned into a product.
hook: Larry Ellison's first product skipped a number on purpose. In 1979 his tiny company shipped its database as ==Version 2==. As he later said with a laugh: "Who in the world would buy software called Version 1 from four guys in California?" He had helped start that company with just ==$1,200==. Then on 10 September 2025, aged 81, a jump in Oracle's shares added about ==$89 billion== to his fortune in a single day, a record on Bloomberg's rich list, and for a few hours he was **the richest person alive**.

glance.label: Born
glance.value: 17 August 1944, New York City (the Bronx, per his Academy of Achievement biography).

glance.label: Grew up
glance.value: A two-bedroom apartment on Chicago's South Side, raised by his mother's aunt and uncle. He did not know he was adopted until he was 12.

glance.label: Education
glance.value: University of Illinois, then University of Chicago. He left both without a degree and says he never took a computer science class.

glance.label: First jobs
glance.value: In California, technician work at Fireman's Fund and Wells Fargo, then programming at Amdahl and Ampex.

glance.label: First company (age)
glance.value: Software Development Laboratories, later Oracle, in June 1977. He was 32 and put in $1,200.

glance.label: Main company today
glance.value: Oracle. Executive Chair and Chief Technology Officer since September 2014, after 37 years as CEO.

glance.label: Source of wealth
glance.value: About 40% of Oracle, plus nearly 50% of Paramount Skydance. Forbes put him at $171.6 billion on 1 November 2026, against more than $400 billion in September 2025. By September 2026 he had pledged 413 million Oracle shares against personal loans.

glance.label: Children
glance.value: Forbes lists four. Two work in public: David Ellison, who heads Paramount, and Megan Ellison, who founded Annapurna Pictures.

glance.label: Lives in
glance.value: Manalapan, Florida, USA, according to Forbes. In December 2020 he told Oracle staff he had moved to Hawaii, to work from Lanai.

glance.label: Known for
glance.value: Founding Oracle, maker of the first commercial SQL relational database, two America's Cup wins (2010 and 2013), and owning 98% of the island of Lanai.

contact.howToReach: No personal email, phone number or confirmed personal social account is published for Larry Ellison, so ignore any site selling his "verified email". If you are a founder, the honest door is Oracle's startup page and free cloud tier; if your work fits what he funds today (health, food, clean energy or government AI), write to the Ellison Institute of Technology, and if you are a student, look hard at the fully funded Ellison Scholars places at Oxford. Press goes to Oracle Public Relations and shareholder questions go to Investor Relations. The Corporate Secretary route is only for genuine issues about Oracle, so a pitch deck sent there or to the Austin head office is unlikely to get anywhere, and neither is a DM to a lookalike account. Write five lines: who you are, what you built, the one number that proves it, the single thing you are asking for, and why this team should care.

factCheck.method: Built primary-first: Oracle's FY2026 Form 10-K and September 2026 proxy statement (roles, head office, phone, board route, pledged shares), Oracle's own contact, media and investor pages, the official sites of EIT and his other ventures, and his own words in the 1995 Smithsonian oral history and his 2007 OpenWorld keynote as reported by the Philippine Star. Life facts were cross-checked across Britannica, the Academy of Achievement, the Computer History Museum and Forbes. Photo authors and licences come from the Wikimedia Commons API. WebFetch got HTTP 403 from some oracle.com pages. Oracle's press, contact, India and startup details were then read from oracle.com through Exa and, for the social links, plain curl, rather than from a separate source, so the fact-checker should re-verify them by hand. Contact-finder and data-broker sites appeared in search results and were rejected as sources.

disputed.note: The Academy of Achievement and Business Insider say the Bronx. The New York Times review of Softwar says the Lower East Side. Britannica says only New York City. We say New York City and credit the Bronx to the Academy.

The Computer History Museum and the 2007 keynote report say there was no V1. Oracle's own timeline says a Version 1 was written in 1978 but never officially released. Either way, the first product sold carried the number 2, so we say it skipped a number.

The Computer History Museum says Ellison bet $2,000. The 2007 keynote report splits it as his $1,200 and Bob Miner's $800. In 1995 Ellison said four people invested $2,000. We use $1,200 as his share of $2,000.
Oracle's timeline names Ellison, Miner and Oates. The Computer History Museum caption also shows Bruce Scott at the founding. The 2007 report says Scott and Oates were hired by Ellison and Miner.

The Academy of Achievement calls his co-founders Amdahl colleagues. Oracle's timeline places them at Ampex, and the 2007 keynote report says he left Ampex for Precision Instruments, which then outsourced work to the new firm. We follow Oracle and his own account.

The 2007 report and Oracle veteran Ken Jacobs say the CIA, with a first sale reported at $48,000. Britannica says the US Air Force at Wright-Patterson Air Force Base. This fragment does not name a first customer.

Bloomberg reported $101 billion during trading and $89 billion at the close, when CNN says he finished about $1 billion behind Musk. CNBC cited a gain of over $100 billion and put Musk above $437 billion on Forbes's tally. We use the closing figure, and 'richest person' holds on Bloomberg's index only, for a few hours.
Forbes says $300 million. Reuters in 2012 said the price was undisclosed, with earlier media estimates of $500 million to $600 million. The glance gives no price.
Forbes now lists Manalapan, Florida. His December 2020 email said he had moved to Hawaii. We found no statement from him about a later move, so the glance gives both with their sources.
Forbes lists four. Wikipedia's infobox says seven, which we could not trace to a reliable source and did not use. Only David and Megan are named here.
Fortune reports Ellison called Nashville the 'world headquarters' in 2024, but Oracle's 2026 10-K and proxy still give Austin as the principal executive office. We list Austin, as filed.

@larryellison carried his rare posts, including the July 2025 Giving Pledge post quoted by Fortune. A March 2026 report from a smaller tech site, not corroborated by major press that we could find, said the profile had vanished. Third-party mirrors show an account under that handle with a 2026 join date and no posts. We could not confirm it is his, so it is not listed.
Commons dates this file 26 January 2016, but it is credited to an older-looking Flickr upload, so year is left null rather than guessed.
